top_choice_rationale: P001 (Melitz and Helpman, B048) is the only awarding proposal on the slate and my preferred configuration. Melitz (2003) is an identifiable originating model. It moved the unit of analysis in trade from the industry to the firm and identified a distinct channel for the gains from trade, namely selection and reallocation toward more productive firms. Its qualitative predictions (selection into exporting, exporter premia, within-industry reallocation after liberalisation) have been tested in firm-level data across many countries for over twenty years, so maturity is largely established. Helpman's work with Melitz and Yeaple on exporting versus FDI, together with his earlier trade theory, makes the two-name credit coherent. The main weakness is priority: Bernard, Eaton, Jensen and Kortum developed parallel firm-level facts and models. The welfare magnitudes also depend on functional-form assumptions such as Pareto productivity. A citation limited to the selection-and-reallocation mechanism and the gains-from-trade framework addresses this only partly, and the committee should state the limit openly. I judge this achievement strong enough to award this year, so no award (P000) ranks below it. I rely on my own knowledge of the literature and have not independently verified any source.
